thread:
maria (Support): FYI escalated ticket C-4412 — customer reports sudden spike in 502/504 + timeouts for hosted inference (us-west-2) starting ~08:10 UTC. ~30% of requests failed. They provided a few request IDs and traces, forwarding now.

alex (SRE): on it. can you drop an example request-id and the error snippet? any auth/billing errors in the same window?

maria (Support): one sample: req=01H7X2K3 errors: gateway 504 -> downstream 504, sometimes 502. Also saw a single 403 billing token error at 08:12 (maybe unrelated). attaching trace: trace://req-01H7X2K3

ops-bot: ALERT: autoscaler-events for namespace "inference" — scaledobject tenant-42: throttleCooldownActive, pendingScaleRequests=3, lastScale=2026-03-17T08:07:12Z

sam (infra): looking at KEDA metrics and HPA for tenant-42. scaledobject appears to have been rate-limited by cooldown and did not scale past 2 replicas. model init times are spiking (~90-130s). readiness probes are failing before model finishes loading, so pods never get Ready.

sam (infra): kubectl snapshot (abridged):
```
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference tenant-42
NAME       REFERENCE                TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
tenant-42  Deployment/tenant-42     78%       2         10        2

$ kubectl get scaledobject -n inference tenant-42 -o yaml | egrep -A3 'cooldown|minReplicaCount|maxReplicaCount'
cooldownPeriod: 30
minReplicaCount: 2
maxReplicaCount: 10
```

sam (infra): also `kubectl describe pods` shows repeated restarts or long Init Containers for `model-init`. image pull ok, but runtime logs show model deserialization and kernel selection taking >60s.

julie (eng-runtime): we pushed a runtime canary at 08:04 that changed kernel-selection and quantization codepaths to improve runtime perf. initial bench looked fine, but I see this might have increased cold-start init time for some model variants. can revert.

alex (SRE): immediate mitigations: 1) manually scale replicas to meet current qps, 2) bump minReplicaCount temporarily, 3) adjust KEDA cooldown/trigger to be less aggressive, 4) route heavy tenants to dedicated capacity if available. can we do 1 & 2 now?

sam (infra): manual scale in progress — `kubectl scale deploy tenant-42 --replicas=6 -n inference`. patching scaledobject -> cooldownPeriod: 15, minReplicaCount: 4. also increased readinessProbe timeout to 120s to avoid killing pods during model init. applying now.

sam (infra): patch commands used:
```
kubectl scale deploy tenant-42 -n inference --replicas=6
kubectl patch scaledobject tenant-42 -n inference --type merge -p '{"spec": {"cooldownPeriod": 15, "minReplicaCount": 4}}'
kubectl patch deployment tenant-42 -n inference --type json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/timeoutSeconds","value":120}]'
```

ops-bot: EVENT: scale up triggered -> +4 pods. readiness events: 3 pods became Ready after model init; 1 pod still initializing.

sam (infra): after scale bump, 5xx rate dropped from ~30% -> ~3% within 90s. customer reports fewer timeouts.

julie (eng-runtime): rolling back the canary to previous runtime image (runtime:v1.22 -> runtime:v1.20) now to see if cold init reverts. will post image/tag when done.

alex (SRE): thanks. julie, can you also add a short-term flag to pre-warm KV cache on POD start for heavy models? that should reduce first-request latency.

julie (eng-runtime): adding a pre-warm flag in a patch; will also prepare a rollback PR and a perf test to replicate tenant burst + model-init latency.

maria (Support): telling customer we scaled them up and implemented a mitigation, offered to migrate them to dedicated capacity if they want guaranteed throughput. they asked about SLA credits — routing to billing.

alex (SRE): post-incident actions: owner=julie (eng-runtime). action items: ["rollback root cause commit","add pre-warm path for heavy models","adjust KEDA defaults for bursty tenants","add alerting on model-init latency and readiness failures","test canary on heavy-model workload before rollout"].

maria (Support): customer update at 08:32 UTC: "timeouts much improved, thanks. still seeing a few slow responses but acceptable for now." they accepted temporary mitigation but requested root-cause timeline.

julie (eng-runtime): will draft repro and timeline by EOD. suspect regression in kernel selection path increased deserialize time for 3/7 model variants.

alex (SRE): leaving channel open for follow-ups. if anyone sees remaining auth 403s (billing token rotate), please paste traces. noting correlation: a 403 at 08:12 might have coincided with a customer token rotation — support to investigate separately.

maria (Support): noted. assigning follow-up tasks in ticket. closing incident channel when debrief scheduled. :white_check_mark:
